To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
MRTF-A is activated by competition with actin-binding proteins for actin binding and that this process is independent of actin filament formation and requires a transferable factor.
WH2 domains, such as those of N-WASP, WAVE2, Spire2, and Cobl, compete for actin binding to the MRTF-A RPEL domain and thereby activate the coactivator for SRF-mediated gene expression.
WH2 domains, which are known to bind actin and promote actin polymerization, can directly activate MRTF-SRP-mediated gene transcription by competing with MRTF for binding to actin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of MRTF-SRP-mediated gene expression.
the regulation of gene expression by actin dynamics.
the regulation of gene expression by the actin cytoskeleton and its role in cell migration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
WH2 domains are able to activate MRTF-SRE activity in the absence of any other factor and that they do this by a mechanism involving the competition of actin for MRTF-SR binding.
MRTF-A is activated by WH2 domains, and that WH2 domains are not only involved in actin polymerization, but also in the regulation of gene expression.
WH2 domains are a new class of activators of MRTF-SRE-dependent gene transcription.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
WH2 domain proteins compete with MRTFs for actin binding, and this is a key step in the regulation of SRF target gene expression.

WH2 domains, which bind actin and promote actin filament nucleation and elongation, can also activate transcription factors by binding actin and competing for the same binding site on the transcription factors.
WH2 domain proteins activate MRTF-SRE by competing with MRTF for actin binding.
The main takeaway from our work is that
WH2 domains are not only actin nucleation-promoters, but also MRTF activators.
WH2 domain proteins, such as Spire2, Cobl, N-WASP, and WAVE2 activate the MRTF-A transcriptional coactivator by a direct competition mechanism.
the WH2 domain is a versatile actin-binding module that can be used for the regulation of actin-dependent processes.
